title: The Unexpected Vow
premise: Jonah Delacroix, a cynical wedding planner nursing a decade-old betrayal, is assigned an anonymous pen-pal exchange meant to pair strangers—except her letters land with Marcus Vane, the rival planner who destroyed her career and now runs the island venue hosting her biggest wedding. Their correspondence, unaware at first of each other's identity, forces both to confess what power cost them. When the truth surfaces mid-season, Jonah must choose between public revenge and the vulnerable sentence she has rehearsed for ten years: 'I forgive you, and I forgive myself.' She speaks it on the dock before the last ferry departs, choosing belonging over justice.
about_author: Theo Kavanagh is a former event coordinator who spent six years orchestrating other people's happy endings before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal cottage, where he insists every love story deserves a storm.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Assignment
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Bitter after losing her firm to Marcus Vane's corporate takeover, Jonah reluctantly joins a writers' retreat pen-pal program, pouring her unspoken grief into letters to a stranger. Meanwhile, she lands the season's most prestigious wedding on Gullwing Island—unaware her anonymous correspondent signs off with phrases that feel hauntingly familiar. Emotional beat: guarded hope flickering through cynicism.

chapters.title: Letters in Enemy Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marcus recognizes Jonah's voice by the second letter but keeps writing anyway, confessing the compromises that made him powerful—and hollow. In person, their rivalry sharpens as wedding preparations collide; on paper, they fall toward tenderness. When Jonah discovers a discarded draft bearing his handwriting, she realizes who her stranger is. Emotional beat: intimacy curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Storm Before the Vows
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Furious, Jonah plots to expose Marcus at the wedding itself, using her planner's control over the ceremony as a weapon. But a storm strands guests, collapses the schedule, and forces them to work side by side through the night to save the day. Watching him give credit away instead of taking it, her rehearsed hatred begins to crack. Emotional beat: rage dissolving into reluctant recognition.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV, closing with Jonah. The wedding succeeds; the season ends; Marcus boards the final ferry expecting silence. Jonah arrives at the dock at the last minute and delivers the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade—not as absolution he can accept easily, but as the vow that frees them both. He misses the ferry deliberately. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a beginning, not an ending.
